title: Monitoring health
description: Is the monitoring itself working, so the other boards and the alerts can be trusted? Open it when an alert says the monitoring is blind (TargetDown, PrometheusRuleFailures, AlertmanagerNotificationsFailing), when a board has gaps, and weekly for the monitoring CT's disk runway.

panels.title: Targets down
panels.description: Scrape targets that fail now, best-effort ones excluded (rule TargetDown: warning after 5 minutes; best-effort targets raise it at info). A failing scrape is a blind spot, not an outage: the board that uses it shows a gap. The `ai` VM is best-effort and off by design, so it is not counted here but is listed in the table below.

panels.title: Rule failures, 10 min
panels.description: Rule evaluations that failed in the last 10 minutes (rule PrometheusRuleFailures, same window). Any failure means an alert is silently broken. Prometheus Status > Rules names the group.

panels.title: Notifications failing, 15 min
panels.description: Notifications Alertmanager could not deliver in the last 15 minutes (rule AlertmanagerNotificationsFailing, same window). Red means Telegram or healthchecks.io cannot be reached: alerts fire but nobody hears them.

panels.title: Watchdog
panels.description: The always-firing Watchdog rule (rules/meta.yml), as Prometheus sees it. FIRING (green) proves Prometheus evaluates rules; NOT FIRING means evaluation stopped or the rule is gone. Whether it reaches healthchecks.io is the dead-man's switch panel further down.

panels.title: TSDB blocks
panels.description: Block storage on disk. Red at 7e9 bytes (rule PrometheusTsdbNearRetentionCap, info after 1 hour): the size cap is near and the oldest data is dropped before 30 days. The cap is 8 GiB, but the CT's disk fills first, see the monitoring CT row.

panels.title: Root disk free
panels.description: Free space on the monitoring CT's root disk, which holds the TSDB, Grafana and the OS. Red under 15 % is rule HostFilesystemFull (warning after 15 minutes); orange under 20 % is a heads-up of this board, not an alert.

panels.title: Disk runway, days
panels.description: Days until the root disk is full if the last 7 days of change continue (linear, capped at 365). Under 30 is worth a look, under 7 is urgent. While the TSDB is still filling toward its 30-day horizon this overstates the risk: read the runway panel in the monitoring CT row before acting. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Prometheus restarts, 7 d
panels.description: How many times the Prometheus process started in 7 days: a reading, with no threshold and no alert. Every restart replays the WAL and resets the pending timers of alerts waiting on `for:`. A count that keeps climbing without a deploy to explain it is worth `journalctl -u prometheus` on CT 120 (crash, out-of-memory).

panels.title: Targets down now
panels.description: Every scrape target that fails right now, with its tier. Empty is good. best-effort targets (the `ai` VM, off unless in use) only raise TargetDown at info; standard and critical raise a warning. A target outside MGMT also needs its hEX scrape rule (runbook: TargetDown).

panels.title: Slowest scrape, by job
panels.description: How long the slowest target of each job takes to answer a scrape. A scrape that reaches its timeout (10 s, 30 s for the SNMP job) fails and becomes TargetDown. A job whose line sits high and flat has a target that is off or unreachable: the `ai` VM, off by design, holds service_dmz near 5 s.

panels.title: Samples per scrape, by job
panels.description: Samples one scrape of each job returns, summed over its targets. It is the weight each job puts on the TSDB: the Kubeletto cluster (service_dmz) and the nodes dominate. A job that doubles overnight is a cardinality problem (see series churn).

panels.title: Rule group evaluation time, share of its interval
panels.description: How long each rule group's last evaluation took, as a share of its 30 s interval. Over 100 % (dashed) the next evaluation is skipped and alerts go late: see missed iterations. The k8s group is the slow one (a few seconds). No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Rule failures and missed iterations
panels.description: Failed rule evaluations (rule PrometheusRuleFailures: an alert that cannot be evaluated never fires) and evaluations skipped because the previous one ran long. Both should stay at zero; the dashed line is the first failure.

panels.title: Notifications sent, by receiver
panels.description: Notifications Alertmanager sends per minute: `telegram` is the chat, `webhook` is the healthchecks.io Watchdog ping. Telegram is quiet unless something fires; webhook is a steady pulse. A flat webhook line is the dead-man's switch starving.

panels.title: Alert delivery failures
panels.description: Alertmanager failing to reach a receiver (rule AlertmanagerNotificationsFailing: token revoked, internet down) and Prometheus failing to hand alerts to Alertmanager. All zero is healthy; the dashed line is the first failure. The failure reason is in `alertmanager_notifications_failed_total{reason}`.

panels.title: Alerts and silences in Alertmanager
panels.description: Alerts Alertmanager holds: active ones are routed, suppressed ones are inhibited (a down host hides its own scrape alerts) or silenced. A silence that is still active after planned work hides real alerts: it should be back to zero. The Watchdog counts as one active alert.

panels.title: Dead-man's switch: Watchdog pings, last 10 min
panels.description: The lab's end of the dead-man's switch: Alertmanager pings healthchecks.io through the `webhook` receiver for the always-firing Watchdog (about one ping per 2 minutes in practice; configured as every minute). healthchecks.io alerts after 10 minutes without one (period 5 + grace 5), which is when this line reaches 0 (dashed). The far end is provable only at healthchecks.io: this shows the pings leave. Mirrors rule Watchdog.

targets.legendFormat: pings sent in the trailing 10 min

panels.title: TSDB: what it holds and how fast it grows
TSDB size against the cap
panels.description: Prometheus's disk use. Blocks are the 30 days of history; the WAL and head chunks are the last couple of hours. The cap line is the live retention.size (8 GiB: the flag value 8GB is read as GiB). The dashed line is 7e9 bytes of blocks, rule PrometheusTsdbNearRetentionCap (info). Past the cap the oldest blocks are deleted early. The root disk is smaller than the cap allows: see the 30-day panel in the monitoring CT row.

panels.title: Head series
panels.description: Series currently in memory. It includes series that stopped receiving samples (for example ended pods) until the next head compaction, so it runs above the number being written now (samples per second times the scrape interval). A step up that stays is new cardinality; a sawtooth that drops every two hours is normal. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Samples appended per second
panels.description: Ingest rate: samples stored per second. It tracks the scrape targets (about the total of Samples per scrape divided by 30 s). A sudden drop is missing scrapes; a sudden rise is a job that added series. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Series churn
panels.description: New series per second against series garbage-collected. Created staying high means label values keep changing (pod names, ephemeral ports) and the head carries many dead series; removed jumps at each 2-hourly head compaction. The scrape_series_added series says which job creates them. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: TSDB housekeeping failures
panels.description: Failed compactions, truncations, checkpoints and block reloads, and WAL corruption. Each is zero on a healthy Prometheus; a compaction that fails keeps retrying and the head grows until the disk is full. The dashed line is the first failure. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: CPU, the CT and Prometheus
panels.description: Share of the CT's 2 cores in use, and the part Prometheus accounts for. Grafana, the blackbox, SNMP and PVE exporters are not scraped for CPU, so the gap between the lines is them plus the OS. Sustained near 100 % delays scrapes and rule evaluation. No alert mirrors it (HostCpuHot is a temperature rule for the Proxmox nodes).

panels.title: Memory, the CT and Prometheus
panels.description: Memory the CT uses (total minus available) and Prometheus's share, with the line where less than 10 % is left (rule HostMemoryLow, warning after 15 minutes). Swap in use means the CT has been short of RAM. Prometheus grows with head series.

panels.title: Pressure stall time
panels.description: Saturation: the share of time at least one task in the CT waited for CPU, disk or memory (kernel pressure stall information). Near zero is healthy; io climbing means compaction or a slow shared disk is stalling Prometheus, memory above a few percent means it is being squeezed. No alert mirrors it.

panels.title: Root disk over 30 days: used, TSDB, everything else
panels.description: What fills the CT's root disk, over the last 30 days whatever the dashboard range. The TSDB grows until it holds a full retention window; everything else is flat (about 5 GB). Prometheus deletes whole 3-day blocks once they are older than 30 days: the first (the small early days, about 120 MB) is due around 2026-11-12, so the line keeps rising until then and should flatten and fall as the heavier days age out. The disk has only about 7 GB for the TSDB, so the 8 GiB size cap can never be reached: HostFilesystemFull (under 15 % free) fires at about 5 GB of blocks, long before PrometheusTsdbNearRetentionCap (7e9 bytes of blocks).

panels.title: Disk runway, days until full
panels.description: Days until the root disk is full if the trend of the last 7 (or 30) days continued linearly. Not a compaction sawtooth (that is the few-hundred-MB wiggle every couple of hours): the slope is steady and all of it is the TSDB filling its 30-day window (see the 30-day panel). A linear runway overstates the risk: retention deletes its first block around 2026-11-12, and an estimate from the daily block sizes puts the low point near 19-20 % free around 2026-11-15 (about 0.5 GB above the 15 % alert), then a recovery to about 24 % by early December. Check that against this panel. Dashed lines: 30 and 7 days. HostFilesystemFull (under 15 % free) is the alert.
